_comment: Asserted byte sizes for istor.fyi's artifact. verify-budget.py fails the build when any of these moves, so a regenerated crop or re-subset font cannot quietly make the site heavier than SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §12.1 says it is. Updating a number here is meant to be a deliberate two-file commit: this file and the design plan's table. Values were measured from disk on 2026-09-19, not transcribed.

totals._note: The payload SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §12.1 prints as 452 KB / 704 KB of exhibits. The plan's table is an estimate carried from the specification; these are the measured values, and on 2026-09-19 the plan's table was re-baselined to match them — the two are one commit. phone_1x is the 1x ASSET payload (exports + ground + the three fonts) and deliberately excludes the document, which is asserted separately under `document` below. RE-BASELINED AGAIN 2026-09-19, for the phone crops: phone_1x 194,064 to 237,991 (+43,927), retina_2x 388,356 to 500,885 (+112,529), and `exports_all_36` becomes `exports_all`, because the set is now 52 files rather than 36 and a key that counts is a key that lies if it keeps its old name. These are the sums of the files the artifact actually carries, recomputed by verify-budget.py rather than typed, and they rise because four exhibits gained a second, genuinely different crop — not because anything got heavier. A phone now requests the 600px crop in place of the 1200px one for those four, so what a device downloads falls while the set's total rises; the totals are an inventory, not a transfer size, and that was already true of phone_1x before today.

document._note: The design plan's payload table omits the document. index.html is real weight and it arrives first, so it is asserted here rather than merely reported. Two numbers, asserted two different ways, and the difference is deliberate. index_html_bytes is a property of the DOCUMENT alone — the artifact is LF-only, so it is identical on every platform — and it is asserted exactly: an edit to the copy deck, or to the stylesheet's CODE rather than its comments, moves it and is meant to. index_html_gzip_ceiling is a property of the document AND of the zlib that compressed it, and Python does not promise byte-stable output across versions, so it is a ceiling with room in it. HISTORY. It read 18,051 B gzipped off 44,812 B raw for all of v1. On 2026-09-19 the first CI run failed a document it had not touched — the artifact was byte-identical to the reviewed one and only the compressed figure differed, 13,722 B on CI's Python 3.12.14/Linux against 13,772 B here on 3.14/Windows, off the same input. A gate that fails on the compressor rather than on the site teaches its reader to ignore it, so the exactness moved to the number that can carry it. RE-BASELINE FOR V2. Both numbers moved: 62,543 B raw, 18,046 B gzipped. The document grew by 17,657 B because the page did — v1 was a static essay with three bitmaps and v2 is twelve acts. The growth is itemised, and none of it is accidental: the inline stylesheet went 15,054 B of code to 19,890 B (five compositions instead of one, a replica window, an accordion, a ring plate, and the motion block), and the markup went roughly 28 KB to 39 KB (the hero's live DOM replica, which is what lets the page perform the product rather than show a picture of it, plus a second smaller replica in the close, which is what Thoria chose over a bitmap there, plus seven FAQ items). The 4,866 B poster replica is the largest single addition and it is a decision, not drift. The compression ratio did NOT get worse — 30.7% under v1, 28.9% now — so this is a longer document, not a harder one, which is what the ceiling is here to distinguish. The ceiling sits 373 B over the highest figure seen, 2.1%, about five times the 50 B spread measured between the two toolchains: room for a zlib to differ, not for the document to change. It is the compression this check fixes, not the compression a visitor receives — GitHub Pages sets that — so this is a floor on the document's weight and a tripwire on it changing. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the Act 8 clearance). 67,326 B to 67,340 B raw; the ceiling holds, at 19,150 B measured against 19,350 B. The 14 B is one declaration: `.plate-inner`'s `padding-block-start` moved from a fixed `150px` to `calc(13.5% + 56px)`, which is 13 B of longer value and 1 B for the blank line the edit left above the rule. That the document moved by exactly that much, and by nothing else, was measured rather than assumed: this build's own `inline_css()` was run over `HEAD:Source/styles.css` and over the working copy, and the diff of the two stripped stylesheets is that one declaration. The raw figure is what moved, so the raw figure is what was re-baselined. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the ring's holes become visible). 67,340 B to 67,544 B raw (+204) and the gzip ceiling 19,350 B to 19,650 B, against 19,242 B measured. The +204 is 203 B of inlined figure and 1 B of stylesheet: `calendar-ring.svg` went 1,318 B to 1,521 B because the dashed circle's stroke changed from `var(--rule)` to `var(--ink-3)` and the two comments that explain it grew with it, and `.plate-inner`'s clearance moved `13.5%` to `24%`. The ceiling MOVED UP for the first time, and deliberately: it existed as a floor on the document's weight with room for a compressor to differ rather than for the document to change, it sat 108 B over the measured figure after this change, and 108 B is under three of the 50 B toolchain spreads it was sized to absorb. It is now 2.1% over the measurement again, the same margin it carried when it was written, so it keeps meaning what it meant. A ceiling that is silently eroded by successive re-baselines stops being a tripwire, which is why this one is recorded rather than nudged. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the reading list). 67,544 B to 71,933 B raw, and the ceiling 19,650 B to 20,480 B against 20,300 B measured. The +4,389 raw is the close's new footer: sixteen links into the carried library, four column heads, a lede, and the comment that explains the block. The ceiling moved to a ROUND number on purpose, 20 KiB, rather than to another 2.1% margin. Three re-baselines in one night is the signal: a ceiling that has to be edited on every commit that touches the document is not guarding the compressor any more, it is tracking the document, and the exact raw assertion above already does that job. At a round 20 KiB it is 180 B over this measurement and will not need touching again until something adds a tenth of a document at once, which is the class of change it exists to catch. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the markup stops shipping its comments). 71,933 B to 63,175 B raw, a **fall of 8,758 B**, and the ceiling 20,480 B to 18,432 B against 17,519 B measured. The fall is one build change: `Source/index.html` carried 21 html comments, 7,768 B, 18.3% of the document, and every visitor downloaded them. Gzipped they were 2,348 B of 12,249, or 19% of the compressed document, which is the number that says they were not trivia. The stylesheet had already solved this exact problem and said so in the header it ships, so this is that rule finally reaching the file it was never applied to. `Source/index.html` still carries all 21 comments; nothing was deleted, only unshipped. The ceiling came DOWN with the measurement rather than staying loose: 20 KiB was sized for a 71 KB document whose tenth is 2 KB gzipped, and at 17.5 KB it would have stopped being able to see that class of change. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (C1 becomes full-bleed). The raw tripwire moved 63,175 B to 65,447 B and the ceiling did NOT move: 18,085 B measured against 18,432 B, 347 B of room, 1.9%, the same margin the round 20 KiB figure was sized with. The +2,272 was measured rather than reasoned about, by rebuilding HEAD into a throwaway tree (`git archive HEAD Source Assets OldVersion`, then the build) and diffing the two artifacts: HEAD builds 64,249 B raw and 17,842 B gzipped, the working tree builds 65,447 B and 18,085 B, so this change is +1,198 raw and +243 gzipped. The other +1,074 raw was ALREADY IN HEAD AND ALREADY FAILING THIS ASSERTION. The parallax commit shipped it, and the budget was read through a pipe, so the exit code that came back belonged to grep and not to the verifier: a gate whose failure can be lost in a pipeline reports ok when it is not. This re-baseline therefore covers two commits, and the second is the one worth looking at, 1,074 B of unexamined document against 1,198 B of examined. +46 B, same night, same act: `html` gains `scrollbar-color: var(--ink-3) transparent`, because the UA's white scrollbar track was a bright stripe down the right edge of a first screen that is now deep teal. One declaration, 11 B gzipped, and the comment above it is stripped like every other stylesheet comment. RE-BASELINE AND RE-SIZE, 2026-09-19 (the rail becomes a table of contents). Raw 65,493 B to 66,726 B (+1,233) and the ceiling 18,432 B to 20,480 B, against 18,417 B measured. This is the first time the ceiling has had to MOVE UP rather than merely be re-measured, and it needs justifying, because a ceiling that is raised whenever it is reached is not a ceiling. It was 18,432 B because the document was 17,519 B when the shipped-comment change landed, and 18 KiB was the round number about a tenth above that. The document is now 18,417 B, so the same rule gives a round 20 KiB again: the ceiling returns to the value it held before the comment change, which is the honest way to read it, one ceiling re-sized twice rather than a number being chased. What forced it was not this change but this change's last byte: it left FIFTEEN bytes of room, and the measured spread between two toolchains compressing the same input is around fifty. A ceiling inside the compressor's own noise fails a document nobody touched, which is the failure this file's history already contains once. It is also worth saying what the +1,233 is: 1,187 B of inlined stylesheet code (the rail's pill, which is real shipped code) plus 46 B of document. The script that drives the rail is inside the document and is most of the rest; its reasoning is in a comment that does not ship. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the close gets a horizon). Raw 66,726 B to 68,646 B (+1,920) and gzip 18,417 B to 18,844 B (+427), measured the same way as the last one: HEAD rebuilt into a throwaway tree diffs against the working tree, so the two numbers are artifacts and not arithmetic. The ceiling does NOT move this time, and the difference is that this change was measured before it was made rather than after: 20,480 B against 18,844 B leaves 1,636 B, which is 8.7%, and the rule that sized it wants about a tenth. Of the +1,920 raw, 1,459 B is the horizon element itself. It is an SVG that the build inlines, so it is document weight rather than an asset request, and that was worth 1.5 KB only because the figure is ONE dashed circle and a stroke stack: 355 holes cost the same bytes as one, because a dash array IS the hole pitch. The plate 900px above it holds the identical 355 holes in 20 KB of markup. The remaining 461 B is the rule that places it, its `max-width: none` (the global `img, svg` rule was capping a 100vw bleed at its containing block) and the include's move inside the wordmark, which is literally nothing: the marker goes in one line either way. What is NOT in these bytes is the reasoning, which lives in make-poster-horizon.py and in the note above the rule, both of which the build strips. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the phone crops). Raw 68,646 B to 70,211 B (+1,565) and gzip 18,844 B to 18,999 B (+155), measured the same way: HEAD rebuilt into a throwaway tree, artifacts diffed. The whole delta is eight `<source>` elements, four exhibits times two formats, each carrying a media query, a type and an intrinsic width and height because a phone crop is a different crop and not a different encoding — density belongs in srcset, art direction belongs in a media query. That is 1,565 B of markup to stop the app's own text arriving at 7.6px on the phone the page is most likely to be read on, which is the cheapest legibility this page has bought all night at 0.1 B per pixel of app text recovered. The ceiling does not move: 20,480 B against 18,999 B is 1,481 B of room, 7.2%, and the assets are not in these bytes at all — they are under `files` and `totals`. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the hero answers back). Raw 70,211 B to 73,264 B (+3,053), gzip 18,999 B to 19,583 B (+584), and the ceiling holds at 897 B of room. The addition is the hero window's own controls: a chip row and two more answers, one of them the refusal, plus the script that switches between them. Measured rather than reasoned about, as usual, and the per-part split is worth having, because the two halves behave differently under compression: the markup is the three questions and two answers, and the script is ~1,400 B that gzips to almost nothing because it is code with repeated tokens. The gzip room left is now 897 B, 4.4%, down from 7.2% and under the tenth this ceiling was sized with. It still passes and is NOT being raised: the next change that adds a section rather than a sentence should re-size it deliberately, with the reason, the way the earlier re-sizes in this note did. THE SCRIPT IS ITS OWN NUMBER NOW, and the reason is in `inline_js_bytes` below: this change also removed 1,250 B of shipped prose from the script, so the script ends this goal 589 B LIGHTER than it began while gaining a feature. That is the shape a budget should have. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the door to the library). Raw 73,264 B to 73,313 B, +49 B, gzip unchanged in kind at 19,583 B, and this is the smallest re-baseline in this note by an order of magnitude, which is the point: the page gained a door to all seventy-five carried articles for one sentence. The reading list's lede now reads "These are the ones to start with, or [see all seventy-five](/library/)", because the sixteen links below it were the only route into the library and the comment above them explains why there are sixteen rather than seventy-five: a footer that lists everything is a sitemap, and the author of a sitemap is a crawler. A single link to a generated directory keeps that reasoning intact and gives the reader what the crawler already had. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (a caption stops being a graphic). 73,313 B to 73,315 B, +2, and the two bytes are worth accounting for because the change behind them is a colour: the ruler's scale label moved from `--ink-3` to `--ink-2`, which is one character longer, and the comment added above the token block is stripped by the build, so what is left of four lines of explanation is a blank line. The finding came from an audit rather than from reading: a WCAG AA pass over every text element on the page, at 1440 in 15 viewports, measured the label at 3.12:1 on --paper where 15px needs 4.5. The token was taken from the app's own palette, where `--ink-3` is a label grey the app really uses, and it is a fine GRAPHIC at that ratio: it still draws the rail, the track and the scrollbar. What it cannot do is be the colour of a sentence, and the token block now says so where before it said "labels and captions", which is how the mistake got made. --ink-2 is the page's own secondary ink and documented as >= 4.5:1 on the same ground; it measures 5.71:1, and the strong lead-in beside it still outranks it. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the library gets the control its stylesheet was waiting for). page_bytes 585,169 B to 599,194 B, exactly +14,025, which is 75 pages x 187 B, and the 187 is worth itemising because it is the whole cost: 143 B of button in the header and 44 B of script tag in the head. The button is a real control that was designed and never shipped: styles.css has carried `.theme-toggle`, `.icon-moon` and `.icon-sun` rules since the library was built, DESIGN.md documents the stamp they were meant to pair with, and the only theme a reader could reach was their own operating system's. `/theme.js` writes the choice the stylesheet already has a rule for. The icons are the one place this note argues for the cheaper shape over the obvious one. The same two Lucide glyphs as inline SVG would be about 320 B of markup in each of 75 headers, some 24 KB for 16px of drawing, so they ship once as two masks and the button tints them with currentColor. /styles.css grew 36,191 B to 39,119 B (+2,928). The two icon masks are 698 B of that, measured on their own lines; the rest is the toggle's own rules, the `hidden` guard that keeps an unscripted button off the page, a focus ring that follows the button's shape rather than squaring it, and the comment this file ships alongside every rule it has, which is where all of that is argued. Two of those were found by looking rather than by reading: the guard, because `.theme-toggle` sets a `display` and a `display` beats the `hidden` attribute, and the ring, because the global `:focus-visible` rule squares a control's corners to 2px and an outline follows the element's radius. index_bytes 27,094 B to 27,281 B, and the identical +187 is the assertion quietly proving itself: the index lifts its header and now its script tag from a real page, so it cannot dress itself in furniture the pages do not have. page_count is unchanged at 75 and the new file is asserted on its own: /theme.js, 3,924 B, one shared file because 75 copies of the same 3.9 KB would be 294 KB of duplicated bytes and a fix would be 75 edits. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the project log catches up with the repository). page_bytes 599,194 B to 600,782 B, +1,588, and this one is the most ordinary kind of re-baseline in the note: a carried page got longer because it says more. /changelog/ is the site's own project log, its lede promises dated work newest first, and its newest entry was 2026-09-17 while the repository has 23 commits dated 2026-09-19. A page that promises a log and stops two days short is not missing a sentence, it is breaking its own claim, so the day got an entry: the v2 rebuild and the reason for it, the three gates, the library's door and its corrected release claims, the exhibit audit, the phone crops and what they did to what a phone downloads, the close's horizon, the hero's third question, and this theme control. Two smaller things moved with it. The entry is the first new *prose* this budget has carried since the copy gate landed, so it is also the gate's first real test rather than its synthetic one, and it fired: my first sentence reported the library's corrected release claim in the claim's own words, and the detector cannot tell a report from a claim. The sentence was rewritten to make the same point without the phrase, which is the right fix, because an allow-list entry here would have bought a permanent hole in the check for a sentence that was mine to reword. And /changelog/ plus the home page plus the eight pages whose copy was corrected moved their lastmod dates to 2026-09-19, with the rule now written into sitemap-dates.json: a date moves when what a page SAYS changes, not when the template it renders through does, which is why the other 65 library pages kept their dates while gaining a header control and a footer link.
document._note_script: The page's one inline script, asserted exactly for the same reason index_html_bytes is: it is a property of the file, platform-independent, and an edit to it is meant to move this number. It exists because the design plan's §7 carried a JS budget of 4 KB that nothing checked, and by 2026-09-19 the page shipped 5,599 B — 1,503 B over, of which 1,250 B was `//` prose shipping to every visitor and being parsed as script. The comments moved into the note above the inline script, which the build strips like any other markup comment, and the hero's controls were added inside what that freed. What remains over 4 KB is CODE for three jobs §7's table did not have when the budget was written: the rail's current-section tracking (M1c), the close's parallax (M6, second half), and the hero's own controls (M9). That is a reason to state the number, not to raise a ceiling, so §7 now points at this assertion and the figure is 5,010 B.

library._note: The carried library (SITE_BUILD_PLAN.md §5). Pages are asserted as a count and a total, not file by file — their bytes change the moment anyone edits a summary, and 75 rows of page sizes would assert nothing worth failing over. Shared assets are exact. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the release claims come off the library). 583,864 B to 582,169 B, a FALL of 1,695 B, and it is worth saying why a fall was re-baselined rather than celebrated as a win: the total is a tripwire on the artifact, not a score, and a page that gets shorter by deleting a false claim is not leaner, it is just different. What moved is eight comparison pages' copy, under the rule stated in SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §10.4 that nothing on this site may claim the source is available until it is. The landing page had obeyed it and the library had not: eight pages called Istor open source and MIT licensed, several tables wrote "Free, open source" in its Price cell, and every one of the 75 offered a "Download" whose link pointed at a releases page GitHub reports as empty. The net is a loss because the honest sentences are shorter than the claims they replace, which is the usual direction when a sentence stops promising something. This note is the only record of the delta that the assertion cannot see on its own: page_count is unchanged at 75, and it should be, because no page was added or removed — the fix was to what the pages say. RE-BASELINE, 2026-09-19 (the door to the library). page_bytes 582,169 B to 585,169 B, exactly +3,000, which is 75 pages x 40 B: the footer gains one link, "All pages", to /library/ on every carried page. Thirty-two bytes of it is the anchor and eight the indent, and it is the only change to the 75 — the index itself is NOT in this number, because the index is not an article and LIBRARY_TOC in the verifiers keeps it out; its bytes are asserted on their own as index_bytes, which is the honest place for generator output. /styles.css moved separately, 35,522 B to 36,191 B (+669): the index needed four declarations for its list, and they went into the library's own stylesheet with its own tokens rather than into a second file or an inline style block.
